hints: Decompose the rational expression as $\dfrac{A}{x+1}+\dfrac{B}{3x+1}$ before integrating both sides.
Combine the resulting logarithms and use $x=1$, $y=1$ to determine the constant of integration.
Rearrange to an exact expression for $y$, substitute $x=3$, and simplify without converting logarithms or radicals to decimals.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in the differential equation $(x + 1)(3x + 1)\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = y$ by dividing both sides by $y(x + 1)(3x + 1)$:
$$\dfrac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \dfrac{1}{(x + 1)(3x + 1)}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Set up the integrals on both sides:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int \dfrac{1}{(x + 1)(3x + 1)}\,\mathrm{d}x$$
The left side integrates directly to:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \ln y$$

Decompose the integrand on the right side into partial fractions:
$$\dfrac{1}{(x + 1)(3x + 1)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 1} + \dfrac{B}{3x + 1}$$
Multiply through by $(x + 1)(3x + 1)$ to obtain the identity:
$$1 = A(3x + 1) + B(x + 1)$$

Find the constants $A$ and $B$ by substitution:
Substitute $x = -1$:
$$1 = A(3(-1) + 1) + B(0) \implies 1 = -2A \implies A = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$
Substitute $x = -\dfrac{1}{3}$:
$$1 = A(0) + B\left(-\dfrac{1}{3} + 1\right) \implies 1 = \dfrac{2}{3}B \implies B = \dfrac{3}{2}$$

Substitute $A$ and $B$ back and integrate each term step by step:
$$\int \left( -\dfrac{1}{2(x + 1)} + \dfrac{3}{2(3x + 1)} \right)\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(x + 1) + \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\ln(3x + 1) + C$$
$$= -\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(x + 1) + \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(3x + 1) + C$$

Combine the logarithmic terms using laws of logarithms:
$$\ln y = \dfrac{1}{2}[\ln(3x + 1) - \ln(x + 1)] + C = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\!\left(\dfrac{3x + 1}{x + 1}\right) + C$$

Use the initial condition $y = 1$ when $x = 1$ to evaluate the constant $C$:
$$\ln(1) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\!\left(\dfrac{3(1) + 1}{1 + 1}\right) + C$$
$$0 = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\!\left(\dfrac{4}{2}\right) + C = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(2) + C \implies C = -\dfrac{1}{2}\ln(2)$$

Substitute $C$ back into the solution and simplify using logarithm rules:
$$\ln y = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\!\left(\dfrac{3x + 1}{x + 1}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(2) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\!\left(\dfrac{3x + 1}{2(x + 1)}\right)$$
Exponentiate both sides with base $\mathrm{e}$:
$$y = \exp\!\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\ln\!\left(\dfrac{3x + 1}{2(x + 1)}\right)\right] = \sqrt{\dfrac{3x + 1}{2(x + 1)}}$$

Substitute $x = 3$ to find the exact value of $y$:
$$y = \sqrt{\dfrac{3(3) + 1}{2(3 + 1)}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9 + 1}{2(4)}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{10}{8}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$$
